segments.title: Feed the engine lemma the right vector space
segments.lean:
classical
  -- Port note (Mathlib 09a9e06): instance search no longer unifies the `Module (ZMod 2)`
  -- instance on `V M` with the one `RightRegular.action` was elaborated against, so pass it.
  obtain ⟨E,hE,hB,hG⟩ := @SourceSchedule.episode_linear_graphs Alphabet M (RightRegular.V M)
    (ZMod 2) _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (Pi.Function.module M (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2)) _ T (RightRegular.action M)
segments.note: K = ZMod 2, V = M → ZMod 2, and ρ = right multiplication. That choice is the whole bridge from monoids to linear algebra. (The Lean passes the module instance explicitly; see its port note.)

segments.title: Name the two families of pieces
segments.lean:
let A : M → Language Alphabet := fun d => {w | w∈E∗ ∧ T (FreeMonoid.ofList w)=d}
  let B : M → Language Alphabet := fun f => {w | w∈remainder E ∧ T (FreeMonoid.ofList w)=f}
segments.note: A d: words made of episodes, with value d. B f: leftovers, with value f.

segments.title: A d has height ≤ 3, because it IS a path language
segments.lean:
have hA : ∀ d, HasHeightAtMost (A d) 3 := by
    intro d
    change HasHeightAtMost ({w | w∈E∗ ∧ T (FreeMonoid.ofList w)=d} : Language Alphabet) 3
    rw [←RightRegular.graph_fiber T E d]
    exact hG (RightRegular.basis M 1) (RightRegular.basis M d)
segments.note: graph_fiber turns 'in E∗ with value d' into 'moves basis 1 to basis d', which is what hG bounds.

segments.title: Index the union by the pairs whose product is accepted
segments.note: I is a subtype of M × M, so it is finite — which is exactly what iSup needs. B f has height ≤ 1 from the engine; mono raises it to 3 (1 ≤ 3, so the same witness expression works).

segments.title: Claim: the recognized language is exactly that union
segments.lean:
have heq : ({w | T (FreeMonoid.ofList w)∈F} : Language Alphabet)=
      ⨆ p : I, A p.1.1 * B p.1.2 := by
    ext w
    constructor
segments.note: Prove the two sets equal word by word, one inclusion at a time.

segments.title: ⊆: factor w, and its two values multiply to T w
segments.lean:
· intro hw
      obtain ⟨es,r,hes,hr,hwr⟩ := factor_remainder hE.1 w
      let d := T (FreeMonoid.ofList es.flatten)
      let f := T (FreeMonoid.ofList r)
      have hdf : d*f∈F := by
        change T (FreeMonoid.ofList es.flatten)*T (FreeMonoid.ofList r)∈F
        rw [←map_mul]
        change T (FreeMonoid.ofList (es.flatten++r))∈F
        rw [←hwr]
        exact hw
      apply Language.mem_iSup.mpr
      refine ⟨⟨(d,f),hdf⟩,Language.mem_mul.mpr ⟨es.flatten,?_,r,?_,hwr.symm⟩⟩
      · exact ⟨Language.join_mem_kstar hes,rfl⟩
      · exact ⟨hr,rfl⟩
segments.note: Only hE.1 ([] ∉ E) is used here, not the full prefix-code property.

segments.title: ⊇: a word in any piece has value d·f, which is in F by construction
segments.lean:
· intro hw
      obtain ⟨p,hp⟩ := Language.mem_iSup.mp hw
      obtain ⟨a,ha,b,hb,rfl⟩ := Language.mem_mul.mp hp
      change T (FreeMonoid.ofList a * FreeMonoid.ofList b)∈F
      rw [map_mul,ha.2,hb.2]
      exact p.2

segments.title: Rewrite the language as that union and hand back hU
segments.lean: exact heq.symm ▸ hU

segments.title: Set up
segments.lean:
classical
  let : Fintype Alphabet := Fintype.ofFinite Alphabet
segments.note: Work classically, and treat the alphabet as an explicit finite type.

segments.title: A shift table for every product table
segments.lean:
obtain ⟨g,hg,hs₁⟩ := exists_shift_table (A := M) (K := K) (S := V)
  let β : M → M → (Fin g → M) → V := fun a c => (hs₁ (ClockAffine.productTable ρ a c)).choose
  have hβ : ∀ a c, ShiftTableProperty g (ClockAffine.productTable ρ a c) (β a c) :=
    fun a c => (hs₁ (ClockAffine.productTable ρ a c)).choose_spec
segments.note: exists_shift_table gives a size g and, for each pair a, c, a solution β a c of the shift-table property for ClockAffine.productTable ρ a c (over V).

segments.title: A second shift table, for the observed inner tables
segments.lean:
obtain ⟨g',hg',hs₂⟩ := exists_shift_table (A := M) (K := K) (S := V × K)
  let γ : (M → (V × K →ₗ[K] V × K)) → (Fin g' → M) → V × K :=
    fun ψ => (hs₂ (ObservedInner.table ψ)).choose
  have hγ : ∀ ψ, ShiftTableProperty g' (ObservedInner.table ψ) (γ ψ) :=
    fun ψ => (hs₂ (ObservedInner.table ψ)).choose_spec
segments.note: The same lemma over V × K gives g' and γ, solving the shift-table property for every ObservedInner.table ψ.

segments.title: Enough copies, and the roster
segments.lean:
let κ := Fintype.card (Kind M (V × K) K g')
  obtain ⟨μ,hμpos,hμ⟩ := exists_copies (M := M) (S := V) g κ (by omega)
  let P := Roster M (V × K) K g' μ
  let B := SlotResidues.slotModulus P
  have hB : 0<B := SlotResidues.slotModulus_pos P
  have hμ' : 20*(10000000*Real.log (2*Fintype.card (Tag M V g B))+4*(g+1))+10<μ := by
    simpa only [B,SlotResidues.slotModulus,P,Fintype.card_prod,Fintype.card_fin,κ] using hμ
segments.note: κ counts the kinds of inner table. exists_copies picks a positive number of copies μ; hμ' restates its guarantee as an explicit numeric lower bound on μ. P is the roster with μ copies, and B its slot modulus, which is positive.

segments.title: A robust clock
segments.lean:
let : Nonempty (Tag M V g B) := ⟨Sum.inr ⟨0,⟨0,hB⟩,1,0,0⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨clock⟩ := RobustClock.exists_clock (Tag M V g B) P
segments.note: Exhibit one tag, so the tag type is non-empty; RobustClock.exists_clock then gives a clock for the roster P.

segments.title: Every slot index is used; fix a reference roster entry
segments.lean:
have honto : Function.Surjective (fun i : P => i.1.j) := by
    intro j
    exact ⟨(⟨j,0,0,fun _ => 1,fun _ => 0⟩,⟨0,hμpos⟩),rfl⟩
  let reference : P := (⟨⟨0,by omega⟩,0,0,fun _ => 1,fun _ => 0⟩,⟨0,hμpos⟩)
segments.note: honto: the map from roster entries to their slot index is onto. reference is one particular entry.

segments.title: Early and late schedules
segments.lean:
obtain ⟨S⟩ := exists_early (Alphabet := Alphabet) clock B (Fintype.card M) hB
    (fun i : P => i.1.j) honto (SlotResidues.reserved P)
  obtain ⟨L⟩ := S.exists_full_late hB g
  let A := S.parameters g L hB
segments.note: exists_early builds an early schedule S from the clock; exists_full_late extends it to a full late schedule L. A collects the resulting parameters.

segments.title: The main cut of slot 0 is an offset
segments.lean:
let j : Fin g := ⟨0,by omega⟩
  have hr : (S.cuts g).main j∈(S.cuts g).offsets := by
    simpa only [OuterStream.Cuts.base,Nat.cast_zero,zero_mul,add_zero] using
      (S.cuts g).offset_mem (.inl j) 0 S.R_pos
segments.note: Pick slot j = 0 and check that its main cut is among the offsets, as the next step needs.

segments.title: The outer graph languages have height ≤ 3
segments.lean:
have hG := S.outer_graph_height L hB T ρ β γ
    (SlotResidues.reserved_distinct P) hμ' hβ hγ reference ((S.cuts g).main j) hr
segments.note: outer_graph_height, fed everything built so far, gives hG: a height-≤ 3 bound for every x, y. The 3 in the theorem comes from this step.

segments.title: Affine recovery: from the outer graphs to the linear path languages
segments.lean:
have hlin := AffineRecovery.recovery_height (L.endRule.prefix_code L.lag) le_rfl
    (fun w => (ρ (T w)).toAddMonoidHom) (OuterStream.wordShift A clock T ρ β L.lag) 3
    (fun x y => by
      rw [←OuterStream.wordUpdate_affine A clock T ρ β L.lag]
      exact hG x y)
segments.note: recovery_height turns hG into hlin: the path languages of ρ ∘ T over the late end rule's episodes have height ≤ 3. Its hypothesis is hG, after rewriting with wordUpdate_affine.

segments.title: The episodes: the end rule's complete words
segments.lean: refine ⟨L.endRule.complete L.lag,L.endRule.prefix_code L.lag,?_,hlin⟩
segments.note: Choose E = the complete episodes of the late schedule's end rule. It is a prefix code, and hlin is the third claim; the leftover bound remains.

segments.title: Output 2: leftovers sorted by value have height ≤ 1
segments.lean:
intro d
  exact L.endRule.remainder_fiber_height T d L.lag
    (fun f b he => (S.episode_visible g L hB he).base)
segments.note: remainder_fiber_height gives the bound for each value d; its visibility side condition is episode_visible.

segments.title: Go classical, then split on whether the alphabet has any letters
segments.lean:
classical
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty Alphabet with h|h
segments.note: The only case split in the whole proof.

segments.title: Empty alphabet: L is finite, because the only word is []
segments.lean:
· let : IsEmpty Alphabet := h
    apply HasHeightAtMost.finite L _ 3
    apply (Set.finite_singleton ([] : List Alphabet)).subset
    intro w _
    cases w with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons a w => exact isEmptyElim a
segments.note: A non-empty word would need a first letter, and there are none. So L ⊆ {[]}.

segments.title: Non-empty alphabet: trade the DFA for a finite monoid
segments.lean:
· let : Nonempty Alphabet := h
    obtain ⟨M,hM,hfin,T,F,hTF⟩ := FiniteRecognition.of_regular hL
    let : Monoid M := hM
    let : Fintype M := hfin
segments.note: This is the only place the hypothesis hL : L.IsRegular is used.

segments.title: Rewrite L as the words whose monoid value lands in F
segments.lean:
have heq : L=({w | T (FreeMonoid.ofList w)∈F} : Language Alphabet) := by
      ext w
      exact hTF w
    rw [heq]
segments.note: hTF is the membership equivalence word by word; ext turns that into equality of languages.

segments.title: Every monoid-recognized language has height ≤ 3
segments.lean: exact FiniteRecognition.recognized_height_three T F
segments.note: 996 of the 1,009 declarations main depends on sit underneath this one step.
